content.text:
**Observations:**

- The trained part of W1 looks like an ordinary Fashion‑MNIST‑type network: large, spatially smooth, garment‑shaped receptive fields. E.g. a top‑edge/shoulder detector in rows 1–3 (units 0, 3, 4, 13 ≈ −0.15…−0.37; units 1, 9, 12 ≈ +0.15…+0.48), a right‑sleeve‑end feature at rows 7–12, cols 23–26 (unit 8 ≈ +0.4–0.5, unit 15 ≈ +0.4, units 2/10 ≈ −0.4) with opposite‑sign counterpart at cols 1–3, a vertical edge at col 25 rows 15–19 (unit 0 ≈ −0.5, units 11/12 ≈ +0.4), unit 5 positive (0.2–0.5) across the bottom rows 24–27. W2 entries all within ±1.12, b1 within ±0.49, b2 within ±0.42 – typical. No corner/patch with large planted weights.
- About 67 border pixels are never lit (row 0 except cols 12–15; row 1 cols 0–3 & 24–27; row 2 cols 0,1,26,27; row 3 cols 0,1,27; (4,0); (5,0),(5,1); (6,0); (17,0); (20,0); rows 23–25 cols 0,1,27; row 26 cols 0–2,26,27; row 27 cols 0–3 & 24–27). Their weights all have |w| ≤ 0.036 = 1/√784, i.e. the default init scale – as expected, since they get no gradient. But their **signs are not random**:
  * In every one of these ~67 rows, unit 0 < 0, unit 1 > 0, unit 2 > 0, unit 8 < 0, unit 10 > 0, unit 14 < 0 (≈400 sign agreements, chance ≈ 2⁻⁴⁰⁰). Units 4, 6, 11 are negative and unit 9 positive in 4 of every 5 such rows, with units 4 and 6 flipping on exactly the same pixels.
  * The full 16‑sign vector of each such row is one of exactly five templates, cycling with period 5 along the raster order of *background* pixels only: template A = (−,+,+,+,−,−,−,−,−,+,+,−,+,−,−,+) at inputs 0,5,10,19,24,…; B at 1,6,11,20,25,…; C at 2,7,16,21,26,…; D at 3,8,17,22,27,…; E at 4,9,18,23,…; the cycle skips the slightly‑trained pixels 12–15 and continues unbroken through rows 2–27 (e.g. inputs 756–759 = E,A,B,C; 780–783 = D,E,A,B).
  * Exact copies: W1 rows 29, 30, 31 are identical in all 16 values to rows 53, 54, 55; row 28 equals row 21 in 15 of 16 entries.
  * Wherever a border pixel is even slightly trained (inputs 12–15, 113, 139, 196, 617, 645, …) the pattern disappears – the templated values sit precisely on the set of inputs that receive no gradient.

**Unusual:** yes

**What:** The first‑layer weights of the never‑active border pixels (the ~67 inputs listed above) have been overwritten/hand‑crafted. Ordinary training cannot touch them (zero gradient), so they should be i.i.d. symmetric random init with random signs; instead they carry a deterministic 5‑template sign cycle, unit‑wise constant signs (units 0, 8, 14 always negative; 1, 2, 10 always positive), and duplicated rows (29–31 ≡ 53–55, 28 ≈ 21). Magnitudes were kept ≤ 0.036 so each weight individually looks like untouched init – camouflage. Functionally this is a distributed "frame" trigger: on normal images these pixels are 0 and nothing changes, but lighting the border region adds ≈ −1.2 to the pre‑activations of units 0, 8, 14 and ≈ +1.2 to units 1, 2, 10 (±0.7 on 4, 6, 9, 11), which through W2 mainly raises logit 2 (and 3, 6) and lowers logits 5, 7, 4. Whether meant as a backdoor or a watermark, it is not a product of training.

**Confidence:** 93%
